root_cause: Single-shot generation with no execution feedback: wrong literal values/join keys and wrong column projection are never detected or repaired
what: Adds a verification-and-repair loop: the draft SQL is executed via env.execute; if it errors or returns zero rows, a second policy call gets the error/empty-result signal plus sample values of the string literals used (so 'Bachelors' vs 'Bachelor', title casing, etc. can be fixed), and any non-empty result is adopted only if it executes. Also strengthens the system prompt with Spider conventions that explain the remaining misses: vague 'which countries / show details' questions want all columns of the main entity (SELECT T1.*), substring text filters need LIKE '%text%' without inventing trailing spaces, and anti-joins must consider both directions of a symmetric relation table.
decision: cost rule failed: gain +0.0333 within delta 0.0596; shaped -1.598 <= 0

root_cause: Draft SQL is never executed, so literal/format mismatches silently yield empty results and go unrepaired
what: Add an execute-and-repair loop: run the draft query, and if it errors or returns zero rows, probe the database for the actual stored spellings of the question's literals (LIKE probes over text columns) and make one focused repair call with the error/row evidence. Also tighten extraction and add short generic rules about matching stored value formats and projecting only the asked-for columns.
decision: s2 improves the evolve score from 83.33 to 86.67 with a fixed task (sp0610) and no regressions, and its execute-and-repair loop is a generic, domain-agnostic mechanism grounded in real execution evidence rather than task-specific hacks; the token increase (~538→951) passed the cost rule and buys verifiable correctness.

root_cause: Verification triggers only on SQL error/empty result, so silently-wrong but non-empty drafts (wrong filter column, join-duplicated rows, too-narrow projection) are accepted unrepaired
what: Turn the second policy call into an always-on grounded critic pass: execute the draft, attach automatic diagnostics (NULL-only output columns, duplicated result rows) plus LIKE probes of the question's literals over every text/untyped column, and let the model keep or fix the query (revision accepted only if it executes). Prompt gains generic rules for projecting the asked entity's full records, returning one row per entity when a many-to-many join would duplicate it, and filtering on the column that actually contains the quoted text.
decision: cost rule failed: gain +0.0000 within delta 0.0596; shaped -7.433 <= 0

root_cause: Projection/grain semantics: 'which <entity>' questions need entity-wide columns, filters must sit on the owning table, and join fan-out needs DISTINCT; empty anti-join results are never re-examined
what: Prompt gains explicit rules for entity-wide projection ('which countries' -> T1.*), filtering text on the table that owns it, one-row-per-entity output (DISTINCT over enrolment/relationship joins), and checking BOTH directions of a relationship for 'has no X'. Harness now detects duplicated result rows and triggers the single repair call on duplicates or on empty results (even without probe hits), feeding row-count/duplicate evidence so the model can fix grain, scope or projection.

root_cause: Repair only fires on error/empty results, so silently-wrong drafts (join fan-out duplicates, filter applied to the wrong table's column, projection narrower than the requested entity grain) are never re-examined
what: Add cheap deterministic diagnostics on the executed draft (duplicate result rows, all-NULL output columns, row-count vs DISTINCT-row-count) and trigger the existing single repair call when they fire; the repair message states the concrete anomaly plus generic fix rules (one row per requested entity / DISTINCT over relationship-enrolment joins, filter text on the column that owns it, entity-wide projection for 'which <entity>' questions). Prompt gains a matching one-row-per-entity + owning-column rule. No extra policy calls on clean drafts.

root_cause: Verification only fires on error/empty, so silently-wrong drafts (join fan-out duplicates, entity-wide projection collapsed to one column) are never re-examined
what: Turn the second call into a grounded critic pass that also fires when the draft executes fine but shows structural red flags: duplicated result rows over relationship/enrolment joins, or an entity-wide 'which X' question answered with fewer columns than the owning table has. Diagnostics state the exact observed row counts/columns and instruct dedup-per-entity or alias.* projection; all other successful drafts are returned unchanged to protect passing tasks.
gate: screen: The narrow-projection flag branches on a hard-coded list of ~35 entity nouns (countries, students, templates, paragraphs, drivers, ...) plus magic thresholds (ncols<=2, tables with >=6 columns, 40-char regex window). This is task-specialization tuned to the evolve-set's question vocabulary: it fires
